report.verdict: A clean but revenue-only Q1: LFL NGR +5% to £216.1m (~$287m), digital +6% and Grosvenor +6% (machines +14%) absorbing the first full quarter of 40% Remote Gaming Duty, with FY27 guidance reiterated as "in line with market expectations" — explicitly conditional on no Budget change to Machine Games Duty. The print neither re-rates nor de-rates the equity; the stock remains a binary on the Autumn Budget, where Shore Capital sizes a hypothetical MGD doubling at £35m (~$47m) gross against FY26 underlying operating profit of £78.6m (~$105m). Beneath the headline, growth decelerated through the quarter (first six weeks +8%, full quarter +5%) and Mecca visits fell again.

kpis.delta: Unchanged; conditional on current UK tax regime

summary: **Headline in line, no profit disclosure.** Q1 FY27 (three months to 30 Sep 2026) Group like-for-like NGR +5% to £216.1m (~$287m): digital +6% to £64.9m (~$86m), venues +5% to £151.2m (~$201m). Rank's Q1 statement is revenue-only — no EBITDA, profit, cash or customer-count disclosure — so the quarter is judged on top-line and tone alone. Growth is at the top end of Shore Capital's unchanged 4–5% FY27 LFL NGR assumption.

**Guidance unchanged, but explicitly conditional.** FY27 Group LFL operating profit guided "in line with market expectations" "based on the current industry tax regime in the UK". No division drove a change because there was none; the caveat is the story. Shore Capital holds FY27 adj. PBT at £54.7m (~$73m), modelling a c.£9m (~$12m) YoY operating profit decline (i.e. c.£70m, ~$93m) on a c.£20m (~$27m) net RGD headwind. Company-compiled consensus was not retrieved [unverified].

**Deceleration inside the quarter is the under-reported signal.** At the 13 Aug prelims, the first six weeks of FY27 showed Group NGR +8%, digital +10% and Grosvenor machines +15%. A full quarter at +5%/+6%/+14% implies weeks 7–13 ran at roughly +2–3% for Group and digital on equal-weekly arithmetic (our estimate). Management cited the UK heatwave for Mecca only; nothing was offered for the digital slowdown.

**Digital held up at 40% RGD with marketing cut — but growth halved.** UK digital +6% (Mecca online +7%), international +4%, in the first full quarter at the 40% duty rate (21% to 31 Mar 2026) and with above-the-line marketing "significantly reduced". This compares with +12% in Q4 FY26 (UK +12%) and +13% in Q1 FY26 (UK +15%, Grosvenor online +31%). Grosvenor online growth was not disclosed this quarter — a notable omission for the largest cross-channel brand (£94.6m, ~$126m FY26 NGR).

**Grosvenor is the operating engine.** LFL NGR +6% to £108.1m (~$144m), visits +1%, spend per visit +5%, +10% QoQ on Q4 FY26's Middle-East-affected £98.3m (~$131m). Machines +14% is the fourth consecutive quarter of acceleration (Q3 FY26 +10%, Q4 +12%) following the 850-machine rollout; tables +3% (FY26 flat), electronic +5%. Implied weekly NGR c.£8.3m (~$11.0m) vs £7.6m (~$10.1m) FY26 average and the £9.5m (~$12.6m) medium-term target.

**Three Grosvenor casinos closed** (Swansea, Reading Central, Sunderland) as "no longer economically viable in the medium term", following nine Mecca closures in FY26. Closure costs will land in H1 FY27 separately disclosed items (unquantified) and the LFL base is being re-cut again — estate pruning flatters LFL op profit margin but shrinks the reported revenue base.

**Mecca flat, and visits keep falling.** LFL NGR £32.2m (~$43m), 0% YoY; visits −3%, spend per visit +3%. The visit trend has deteriorated each period (−1% Q1 FY26, −2% FY26, −3% now) and spend-per-visit growth halved from +6%. Weather is the stated cause; the structural attrition of an older customer base is the unstated one. The August target of "double-digit operating profit in 2026/27" (FY26: £8.9m, ~$12m) was not reiterated in the Q1 statement.

**Enracha the quiet compounder.** Spanish venues LFL NGR +7% to £10.9m (~$14m), electronic gaming +11%, consistent with +5% (Q1 FY26), +7% (FY26) and +6% (Q4 FY26); FY26 LFL op profit a record £12.0m (~$16m) at a 26.5% margin — the group's highest-margin unit and, together with Yo digital, a natural hedge against UK fiscal risk.

**Tax is the whole debate.** RGD rose from 21% to 40% on 1 Apr 2026; Rank quantified the gross annual operating profit impact at c.£40m (~$53m) before mitigation (Nov 2025 Budget RNS) and management said in August that "digital profitability will inevitably step down in 2026/27". MGD sits at 20%; Shore Capital estimates a hypothetical doubling to 40% would be a £25m (~$33m) gross hit at Grosvenor and £10m (~$13m) at Mecca — c.45% of FY26 underlying operating profit. Peel Hunt expects the Budget to pass without negative effect.

**CEO messaging is lobbying, not guiding.** Richard Harris: any MGD increase "will increase costs, reduce venue viability, lead to venue closures and job losses, reduce tax receipts and halt investment"; SBC reports he has suggested a hike could close around a third of venues. Rank paid £225.9m (~$300m) in UK/Spanish taxes and duties in FY26 (£198.9m, ~$265m in the UK).

**Cost mitigation: delivered in H2 FY26, nothing new quantified.** The RGD response (ATL marketing cuts, supplier savings, headcount reductions) held FY26 LFL employment costs flat at £270.3m (~$359m) despite c.4% underlying inflation and let FY26 underlying operating profit reach £78.6m (~$105m), +21%, 9.4% margin. FY27 capex is guided to normalise to c.£40m (~$53m) from £50.2m (~$67m), with "further improvement in underlying cash generation". No new programme or target-year savings were disclosed at Q1.

**Capital position (last reported 30 Jun 2026) is comfortable.** Net cash pre-IFRS 16 £56.8m (~$76m); IFRS 16 net debt £147.2m (~$196m) = c.1.1x FY26 underlying EBITDA of £138.3m (~$184m) (our calc), comprising £204.0m (~$271m) leases and £30m (~$40m) drawn on a new four-year £120m (~$160m) RCF against £86.8m (~$115m) cash. FY26 net free cash flow £25.5m (~$34m) after £10.3m (~$14m) SDI cash outflows. Final dividend 2.50p (~$0.033) paid 23 Oct; FY26 total 3.50p (~$0.047), +35%. No buyback; policy is progressive dividend to >35% payout with surplus returns at Board discretion.

**Legacy one-offs still bleeding cash.** FY26 SDIs of £22.9m (~$30m) included the £6.5m (~$8.6m) Spanish payment fraud, a £5.0m (~$6.7m) proposed Gambling Commission settlement for historical Grosvenor venue compliance failings (review period Nov 2024–May 2025), £6.7m (~$8.9m) Mecca closure costs and £3.7m (~$4.9m) restructuring. Management flagged further SDI cash outflows in FY27; the three Q1 casino closures add to the list.

**Medium-term targets stand (as of August).** ≥£100m (~$133m) underlying operating profit; Grosvenor £9.5m (~$12.6m) weekly NGR with +500bps margin; machine NGR ≥£3m (~$4.0m)/week vs £2.2m (~$2.9m) in FY26; ROCE 18.3% in FY26 (+3.2ppt). Shore notes an MGD rise could delay the £100m. Q1 did not restate these.

**Governance remains in transition.** Richard Harris (ex-CFO) became interim CEO on 30 Jan 2026 and permanent CEO on 13 Jul 2026; interim CFO Cliff Baty sits on ExCo but not the Board; Chair John Ott since Nov 2025; Lucinda Charles-Jones left the Board after the 8 Oct AGM, leaving interim Audit (Keith Laslop) and Remuneration (Katie McAlister) chairs and a vacant SID role. AGM resolutions passed comfortably (McAlister re-election 98.2% for). A permanent CFO and SID are overdue.

**Strategy pivot to 'casino-led and bingo-led gaming'.** FY27 initiatives flagged in August — smaller-format, machine-led casino trial on spare licences; Mecca social lounges (Stockton £1.6m, ~$2.1m); Mecca app rollout due complete by end Q1 FY27 and single membership in H1 FY27; YoBingo Portugal; Intelligent Customer Platform — none received a progress update in the Q1 statement.

**Comparables frame the slowdown.** Quarterly Group LFL NGR growth: Q1 FY26 +9%, H1 FY26 +6% (£419.8m, ~$558m), Q4 FY26 +6% (£208.9m, ~$278m), FY26 +6% (£834.1m, ~$1.11bn), Q1 FY27 +5%. Digital: +13%, c.+4% (Q2 implied), +2% (Q3), +12% (Q4), +6%. The Q4 FY27 comp (+12% digital) is the hardest in the year.

**Market reaction: a non-event into a known binary.** Shares were broadly flat early at 74.10p (~$0.99), +0.3% vs the 73.90p prior close, having fallen c.14% over one month, c.23% over three and c.43% over twelve (Shore Capital). At 74p the market cap is c.£347m (~$461m) and EV/FY26 underlying EBITDA c.3.6x on an IFRS 16 basis (our calc) — the Budget is largely priced, which is Shore's point.

**Thesis read-through.** Operationally the equity story is intact: machine-led Grosvenor growth, a UK digital business proven viable at 40% RGD, estate pruning and falling capex driving FCF. But the quarter adds two non-Budget worries — in-quarter deceleration in digital and a third consecutive decline in Mecca visits — and the only catalysts that matter are the Budget (date not confirmed in our sources) and H1 results on 28 Jan 2027.

segments.name: Digital (UK: Mecca, Grosvenor, proprietary brands; International: Yo/Enracha Spain, Portugal)
segments.headline: Resilient at 40% RGD with marketing cut — +6% to £64.9m (~$86m) — but growth halved from Q4 and faded through the quarter; profitability step-down is the FY27 certainty.
narrative: Digital LFL NGR rose 6% to £64.9m (~$86m), the first full quarter under the 40% Remote Gaming Duty regime (up from 21% from 1 April 2026) and with above-the-line marketing "significantly reduced" as part of the H2 FY26 mitigation programme. The UK business grew 6%, led by the Mecca online brand at +7%, with international (YoBingo/YoCasino/YoSports in Spain plus the recently launched Portuguese YoBingo) at +4%. Management framed the UK as continuing "to demonstrate resilient customer metrics despite the higher tax regime", and Shore Capital highlighted growth in first-time depositors. Sequentially the segment was +1.6% on Q4 FY26's £63.9m (~$85m), but the growth rate roughly halved from Q4's +12% (UK +12%) and from Q1 FY26's +13% (UK +15%, Grosvenor online +31%, Mecca online +9%). Digital was 30.0% of Group NGR, broadly unchanged.

The trajectory inside the quarter deteriorated. At the 13 August prelims, the first six weeks of FY27 showed digital +10%; a full quarter at +6% implies the remaining seven weeks ran at roughly +2–3% on equal-weekly arithmetic (our estimate), i.e. back toward the Q3 FY26 run-rate (+2%) that management had blamed on platform stability before the Q4 rebound. Grosvenor online, 13% growth for FY26 and the largest cross-channel brand at £94.6m (~$126m), was not disclosed this quarter; with Mecca (+7%) the only brand called out and the UK at +6%, the inference is that Grosvenor online grew below the UK average. Other proprietary brands (Spin & Win, Lucky Pants; £21.0m, ~$28m, −5% in FY26) were again unmentioned and likely remained in decline despite the brand refreshes.

Marketing is the swing variable, and management is signalling a re-balance: "Our focus on the customer proposition and overall marketing spend balance remains a priority as the wider digital landscape continues to reset." The ATL cuts protected FY26 profit; this sentence reads as acknowledgement that sustaining the top line may require redeploying spend into performance marketing as competitors retrench. Rank does not disclose marketing as a percentage of NGR, monthly actives or ARPU at quarterly points; FY26 showed UK average revenue per customer +10%, with free bets and incentives explicitly maintained (promotional cost is netted within NGR, which Rank defines as GGR less customer incentives). Structural cost drags persist: the statutory RPT levy at 1.1% of GGY (£2.7m, ~$3.6m in FY26) and the online slots staking limit (£4.0m, ~$5.3m profit impact in FY26).

Profitability was not disclosed. FY26 digital underlying LFL operating profit was £37.9m (~$50m), a 15.2% margin, with only one quarter at 40% RGD. Management guided in August that "digital profitability will inevitably step down in 2026/27"; the November 2025 Budget RNS put the gross pre-mitigation annual impact at c.£40m (~$53m) and Shore Capital models a c.£20m (~$27m) net headwind after mitigation. On 6% revenue growth we estimate FY27 digital operating profit of £22–27m (~$29–36m), a 10–11% margin (our estimate), with the Q4 FY27 comparison (+12%) the toughest of the year. Any move by HM Treasury to apply the 40% rate to gross gaming yield rather than gross gaming revenue — Rank's lobbying ask — would be upside not in anyone's numbers.

International grew 4% against a Spanish business that had returned to +13% NGR growth in H2 FY26 after platform capacity constraints were resolved; the slowdown suggests either Spain decelerated or Portugal's start-up is diluting the aggregate — no split was given. At c.£30m (~$40m) annual NGR (Enracha/Yo digital, FY26) international is c.12% of digital, so diversification away from UK fiscal risk remains more narrative than number. Segment guidance is implicit in the Group "in line with market expectations" line; watch the Intelligent Customer Platform implementation, the Gambling Commission's Financial Risk Assessment rollout (industry pressing for further consultation) and whether marketing intensity rises into H2.

segments.name: Grosvenor Venues (UK casinos)
segments.headline: +6% to £108.1m (~$144m) on spend per visit; machines +14% and accelerating for a fourth quarter — the operating thesis, and the MGD exposure, in one segment.
narrative: Grosvenor venues LFL NGR grew 6% to £108.1m (~$144m), with visits +1% and spend per visit +5% — a different mix from Q1 FY26 (+8%, visits +5%, spend per visit +3%), when the £15m (~$20m) Victoria, Edgware Road reopening was driving footfall. Sequentially the segment was +10% on Q4 FY26's £98.3m (~$131m), a quarter in which growth had slowed to +3% as the Middle East conflict hit London table play; some of the QoQ step-up is therefore recovery rather than momentum. Implied average weekly NGR was c.£8.3m (~$11.0m) against £7.6m (~$10.1m) for FY26 and the £9.5m (~$12.6m) medium-term target set at the October 2025 Capital Markets Event, which is paired with a 500bps margin improvement ambition. No London versus rest-of-UK split was given this quarter (FY26: £123.6m / £273.7m, both +5%).

Product mix is moving the right way for margin. Gaming machines grew 14% (Q3 FY26 +10%, Q4 +12%, first six weeks of FY27 +15%), the fourth consecutive quarter of acceleration since the 850 incremental machines were installed across 38 casinos in H1 FY26 with minimal capital. Management reiterates that new machines take two to three years to mature and that weekly machine NGR of £2.2m (~$2.9m) in FY26 should reach at least £3m (~$4.0m); on the Q1 run-rate the estate is tracking toward c.£2.5m. Table gaming grew 3% (flat in FY26; 44% of casino NGR) and electronic gaming 5% (16% of NGR). The shift toward machines and electronic terminals — the most productive assets per square foot — underpins the margin thesis, but it also concentrates the fiscal exposure: FY26 machine NGR of £113.2m (~$151m) sits under Machine Games Duty at 20%.

The estate is being reshaped around machine economics. Three casinos — Swansea, Reading Central and Sunderland — were closed in the quarter as "no longer economically viable in the medium term", following FY26 impairment charges of £9.4m (~$12.5m) against reversals of £3.9m (~$5.2m). Closure costs will fall into H1 FY27 separately disclosed items (unquantified) and marginally reduce the LFL base. In parallel, FY27 brings the trial of smaller-format, machine- and electronic-terminal-led casinos using existing spare licences, a real-time machine loyalty programme trial in H1, and sports betting terminals now in 24 venues. Refurbishment capex is being redirected toward smaller, higher-return schemes after analysis showed these outperform large projects.

On costs and profit, nothing was disclosed for Q1. FY26 Grosvenor underlying LFL operating profit was £35.5m (~$47m), +11%, an 8.9% margin, with employment costs of £161.8m (~$215m) up 2% on National Minimum Wage uplift and the 0.5% RPT levy on GGY. With 6% revenue growth, a semi-fixed cost base that has historically delivered c.60% drop-through, loss-making venues removed and depreciation moderating, we estimate FY27 Grosvenor operating profit of £38–41m (~$51–55m) before any MGD change (our estimate). Shore Capital sizes a hypothetical MGD doubling to 40% at £25m (~$33m) gross for Grosvenor alone — roughly two-thirds of the segment's FY26 profit — which is why the CEO's statement devotes more words to the Budget than to trading.

Regulatory housekeeping continues: the £5.0m (~$6.7m) proposed Gambling Commission settlement relates to historical compliance failings in Grosvenor venues (review period 1 Nov 2024–1 May 2025), with remedial actions substantially implemented in H1 FY26 and facial-recognition entry trials under way. Segment guidance is subsumed in the Group line; management's framing — machines "underlining our confidence in further improvement as we optimise the performance of the machine estate" — is the one unambiguous positive in the release, and the lever on which the £100m (~$133m) Group target depends.

segments.name: Mecca Venues (UK bingo)
segments.headline: Flat at £32.2m (~$43m) with visits −3% — weather is the stated reason, but visit attrition has worsened for three straight periods; the duty-abolition tailwind still points to double-digit profit.
narrative: Mecca venues LFL NGR was flat at £32.2m (~$43m), with customer visits down 3% and spend per visit up 3%. Management attributed the softness in visits to "the prolonged period of hot weather in the UK". The absolute figure is 9% below the £35.5m (~$47m) reported for Q1 FY26 and 9% below Q4 FY26's £35.4m (~$47m), but neither comparison is like-for-like: the nine clubs closed during FY26 (FY26 revenue £12.6m, ~$17m, roughly £3m a quarter) have been removed from the FY27 base, leaving a 41-club estate.

The visit trend is the structural concern beneath the weather. Visits fell 1% in Q1 FY26, 2% across FY26 and 3% now, while spend-per-visit growth has halved from +6% (Q1 FY26 and FY26) to +3%. Shore Capital expects improvement as weather normalises, and the Q2 FY26 comparison was described at the time as "slightly softer", so the H1 optics may recover. But the product mix tells the longer story: mainstage bingo (+12% in FY26) is the reason to visit and is in good health; interval bingo was flat; gaming machines (+6%, 42% of NGR) carry the growth; and 60% of visits are now played on tablets with electronic customers accounting for 80% of mainstage spend. Growth therefore depends on digitising an ageing customer base inside a shrinking estate.

Profit was not disclosed, but the FY27 set-up is favourable in the absence of a Budget shock. FY26 underlying LFL operating profit was £8.9m (~$12m), +107%, a 6.2% margin, with bingo duty abolished from the start of Q4 FY26 — an in-year benefit of £1.6m (~$2.1m) and an annualised FY27 benefit of c.£6.4m (~$8.5m), i.e. c.£4.8m (~$6.4m) incremental. Management said in August the business is "well on track to deliver double digit operating profit in 2026/27"; on flat revenue the duty tailwind alone gets close, and we estimate £10–12m (~$13–16m) (our estimate). That statement was not repeated in the Q1 release. The offset is Machine Games Duty: Shore's £10m (~$13m) gross hit from a hypothetical doubling would exceed Mecca's entire FY26 profit — bingo clubs are the most MGD-sensitive assets in the group.

The initiative pipeline was silent this quarter. August listed the new proprietary Mecca app (rollout across all venues due by end of Q1 FY27), single membership across channels in H1 FY27, the £1.6m (~$2.1m) Stockton social lounge completed in August, self-serve electronic play kiosks, contactless interval bingo and five further external signage schemes; clubs that received machine-area investment grew machine income 9% in FY26 with typical 18-month paybacks. None of this was updated on 15 October — management chose to say nothing about Mecca beyond flat revenue and the weather, which, for a segment management describes as targeting "medium-term cash maximisation", is a disclosure gap investors should press on at the 28 January interims.

points: Absolute figure is 9% below Q1 FY26's £35.5m (~$47m) and Q4 FY26's £35.4m (~$47m), but neither is like-for-like.
Nine clubs closed during FY26 (FY26 revenue £12.6m, ~$17m, roughly £3m a quarter) removed from the base, leaving 41 clubs.

quote.speaker: Management

blocks.heading: Visit trend
blocks.takeaway: Visit attrition has worsened for three straight periods (−1%, −2%, −3%) and spend-per-visit growth has halved from +6% to +3%.
points: Shore Capital expects improvement as weather normalises; Q2 FY26 comparison was "slightly softer", so H1 optics may recover.
Mainstage bingo +12% in FY26 and in good health; interval bingo flat; gaming machines +6%, 42% of NGR, carry the growth.
60% of visits played on tablets, electronic customers 80% of mainstage spend; growth depends on digitising an ageing customer base in a shrinking estate.

blocks.heading: Profit outlook
blocks.takeaway: Bingo duty abolition gives c.£4.8m (~$6.4m) incremental FY27 benefit; we estimate £10–12m (~$13–16m) profit, but MGD doubling would exceed FY26 profit.
points: FY26 underlying LFL operating profit £8.9m (~$12m), +107%, 6.2% margin; duty abolished from start of Q4 FY26 with £1.6m (~$2.1m) in-year, c.£6.4m (~$8.5m) annualised.
August guidance of "well on track to deliver double digit operating profit in 2026/27" was not repeated in the Q1 release.
Shore's £10m (~$13m) gross MGD hit would exceed Mecca's entire FY26 profit — bingo clubs are the most MGD-sensitive assets in the group.

blocks.heading: Initiative pipeline
blocks.takeaway: Nothing on initiatives was updated on 15 October — a disclosure gap investors should press on at the 28 January interims.
points: August listed the proprietary Mecca app (rollout due by end Q1 FY27), single membership in H1 FY27, £1.6m (~$2.1m) Stockton social lounge, kiosks, contactless interval bingo, five signage schemes.
Clubs with machine-area investment grew machine income 9% in FY26 with typical 18-month paybacks.
Management describes the segment as targeting "medium-term cash maximisation".

segments.name: Enracha Venues (Spain)
segments.headline: +7% to £10.9m (~$14m) on electronic gaming +11% — the group's most consistent and highest-margin unit, and its only hedge against UK fiscal risk.
narrative: Enracha venues — nine large multi-game bingo-led venues in Spain combining bingo, electronic roulette, gaming machines and sports betting — grew LFL NGR 7% to £10.9m (~$14m), driven by 11% growth in electronic gaming. The LFL measure excludes FX, so this is local-currency growth. Sequentially the segment was 3.5% below Q4 FY26's £11.3m (~$15m), which looks seasonal rather than a trend break: the growth cadence has been remarkably consistent at +5% (Q1 FY26), +7% (FY26), +6% (Q4 FY26) and +7% now. No visit or spend-per-visit split was disclosed for the quarter (FY26: visits −1%, spend per visit +8%).

Profit was not disclosed, but FY26 underlying LFL operating profit was a record £12.0m (~$16m), +8%, at a 26.5% margin — the highest in the group and roughly a third of Group underlying operating profit from 5% of revenue. The economics rest on gaming machines (46% of revenue in FY26, machine numbers +16% since FY24 with revenue per machine +6%), a bingo product that competitors have withdrawn for economic reasons, and well-invested venues (Sabadell machine-area expansion; the Seville Bingo Boom social format now being copied into Mecca Stockton). The December 2025 payment fraud in the Spanish businesses (£6.5m, ~$8.6m, taken as a separately disclosed item) was a control failure, not a trading one, but it is a reminder that the Spanish units run on a separate platform and control environment.

Strategically, Enracha and the Yo digital brands (combined c.£75m, ~$100m annual NGR and c.£15–16m, ~$20–21m of operating profit in FY26) carry no RGD or MGD exposure and are the reason management keeps emphasising international diversification. At the current scale they offset perhaps a third of the modelled net RGD headwind, so the hedge is partial. Guidance is implicit in the Group line; we would expect FY27 Enracha operating profit of £12–13m (~$16–17m) on mid-single-digit growth (our estimate), with reported sterling figures sensitive to EUR/GBP.

highlights.text: **Grosvenor machines +14%, accelerating for a fourth consecutive quarter** (Q3 FY26 +10%, Q4 +12%) on an estate expanded by 850 machines with minimal capex; weekly machine NGR tracking from £2.2m (~$2.9m) toward the ≥£3m (~$4.0m) target with 2–3-year maturation still ahead.

**UK digital proven viable at 40% RGD**: +6% UK NGR (Mecca online +7%) with ATL marketing cut and first-time depositors growing — the 'can it survive the duty' question answered, even if profit steps down.
**Guidance held with Q1 growth (+5%) at the top of the 4–5% FY assumption**; Shore Capital left FY27 adj. PBT of £54.7m (~$73m) unchanged. Easier Q2 FY26 comparison ("slightly softer") sets up H1.

**Estate pruning is working**: 9 Mecca and 3 Grosvenor closures remove loss-makers from a semi-fixed cost base; Mecca LFL op profit doubled in FY26 to £8.9m (~$12m) with c.£4.8m (~$6.4m) of incremental bingo-duty tailwind still to come in FY27.

**Balance sheet and cash trajectory improving**: net cash pre-IFRS 16 £56.8m (~$76m), new 4-year £120m (~$160m) RCF, capex falling to c.£40m (~$53m) in FY27 from £50.2m (~$67m), progressive dividend (+35% to 3.50p, ~$0.047).
**Enracha +7% with a 26.5% margin** — a consistent compounder outside the UK tax net, and the proving ground (Seville social bingo) for Mecca's format evolution.

lowlights.text: **In-quarter deceleration**: first six weeks +8% Group / +10% digital versus +5% / +6% for the full quarter implies weeks 7–13 at roughly +2–3% (our estimate). Management explained Mecca (weather) but not digital.

**Mecca visits −3%, the third consecutive decline** (−1%, −2%, −3%) with spend-per-visit growth halving to +3%; the heatwave is one-off, the attrition of an older customer base is not. The August 'double-digit profit' target was not reiterated.

**Digital growth halved from Q4 (+12%) and the Grosvenor online brand was not disclosed**; the "marketing spend balance" language hints that the ATL cuts that saved FY26 profit may need partial reversal. Digital profit will step down from £37.9m (~$50m) regardless.

**The equity is a Budget binary and guidance says so**: "based on the current industry tax regime". A hypothetical MGD doubling (Shore: £25m Grosvenor + £10m Mecca, ~$47m gross) equals c.45% of FY26 underlying operating profit; Rank's own November 2025 RGD disclosure was c.£40m (~$53m) gross.

**Revenue-only disclosure**: no EBITDA, profit, cash, actives, ARPU, marketing ratio or net sports/gaming margin — materially thinner than listed peers' quarterly reporting, and it leaves the digital margin trajectory unobservable until 28 January.

**Governance still interim**: permanent CFO and Senior Independent Director vacancies, interim Audit and Remuneration chairs, a proposed £5.0m (~$6.7m) Gambling Commission settlement awaiting finalisation, and a £6.5m (~$8.6m) Spanish payment fraud within the last year.
**SDI cash drag continues into FY27**: FY26 SDIs £22.9m (~$30m) with £10.3m (~$14m) cash out; management flagged further outflows in FY27, to which the Q1 casino closures add unquantified costs.

forecast.intro: Guidance is unchanged in form and substance: at the August prelims Rank said digital profitability would 'inevitably step down' in FY27 on annualised 40% RGD while reiterating the ≥£100m (~$133m) medium-term operating profit ambition; on 15 October it reaffirmed FY27 Group LFL operating profit 'in line with market expectations', with the explicit condition 'based on the current industry tax regime in the UK'. No division moved the guidance; the bridge from FY26 is driven by digital (RGD annualisation) on the downside and Grosvenor machines plus Mecca duty abolition on the upside. Rank does not publish a consensus figure we could retrieve; Shore Capital's unchanged model (adj. PBT £54.7m, ~$73m; LFL NGR +4–5%; c.£20m, ~$27m net RGD headwind) implies underlying operating profit of roughly £70m (~$93m), c.£9m (~$12m) below FY26.

forecast.view: **Next quarter (Q2 FY27, Oct–Dec):** we expect Group LFL NGR growth of **+4–6%** against a comparison management itself called 'slightly softer' — Grosvenor +5–7% with machines still double-digit (the +12% Q2 FY26 machine comp is manageable), digital +4–6% as the back-half-of-Q1 run-rate meets an easier comp (Q2 FY26 digital c.+4% implied from H1 +8%), Mecca 0–2% as weather normalises, Enracha +5–7%. H1 FY27 underlying operating profit should land around **£33–36m (~$44–48m)** versus £40.6m (~$54m) in H1 FY26, with the full RGD step-down visible in digital for the first time. **Full year:** LFL NGR **£865–875m (~$1.15–1.16bn), +4–5%**; underlying EBITDA c.**£128–133m (~$170–177m)** (margin c.15%, down c.150bps); underlying operating profit **£68–72m (~$90–96m)** — i.e. we sit at or marginally below the Shore-implied c.£70m, because we assume some marketing re-investment in H2 and no recovery in Mecca visits. **Leverage direction: improving.** Capex down c.£10m (~$13m), SDI cash outflows of perhaps £8–10m (~$11–13m), dividends c.£16m (~$21m) and no buyback should still lift net cash pre-IFRS 16 from £56.8m (~$76m) toward **£60–70m (~$80–93m)** by June 2027; IFRS 16 net debt stays c.1.1–1.2x EBITDA. **Swing factors:** (1) the Autumn Budget — an MGD increase of any size would cut these numbers by up to £35m (~$47m) gross and trigger further closures; conversely, no change removes the discount the shares carry at c.3.6x FY26 EV/EBITDA (IFRS 16, our calc); (2) whether digital growth re-accelerates or the 'marketing balance' resets margin; (3) the Q4 FY27 digital comp of +12%; (4) Mecca visit recovery and the unrepeated double-digit profit target. All figures above are our estimates, not company guidance.
watch: Autumn Budget outcome on Machine Games Duty (20%) and any RGD base change from GGR to GGY — the single determinant of FY27–28 earnings; the date was not confirmed in our sources.

H1 FY27 results on 28 Jan 2027: first disclosure of digital operating margin under a full 40% RGD run-rate, marketing re-investment, SDI quantum from the three Grosvenor closures, and whether Mecca's 'double-digit' FY27 profit target survives.
Grosvenor weekly NGR and machine NGR versus the £9.5m (~$12.6m) and ≥£3m (~$4.0m) medium-term targets; evidence from the smaller-format casino trial and machine loyalty pilot.
Digital growth cadence into the +12% Q4 FY27 comp, Grosvenor online disclosure, and international (Spain/Portugal) momentum after a +4% quarter.
Mecca visit trend post-heatwave, app/single-membership rollout completion, and interval bingo modernisation.

Governance completion: permanent CFO, Senior Independent Director, permanent committee chairs; finalisation of the £5.0m (~$6.7m) Gambling Commission settlement; Financial Risk Assessment implementation.
